purpose: Optional story-specific History illustrations for editorial and app-integration review; not an approved production media manifest.
distributionScope: Offline school presentation/prototype only. User states this app will not be published and school staff permit public ACLC photographs. Other third-party asset rights remain unverified; credits retained for any wider reuse.

entries.subject: 2022 sonar bathymetry: the lake's northwest basin and connecting channel
entries.locator: Philippine Journal of Science, 2024, Figure 2 (bathymetric map and terrain view)
entries.captionEn: A 2022 sonar survey mapped two basins of Lake Danao and a connecting channel.
entries.altEn: Scientific bathymetric figure showing two basins and depth contours of Lake Danao.
entries.editorialCaution: Obtain publisher/author permission and check third-party satellite-basemap rights; open access alone does not grant reuse. Do not reconstruct exact depths without checking the paper.

entries.subject: Bazzania globuliformis, the exact leafy liverwort named in the History panel
entries.locator: Frahmia 33 (2023), page 37, Plate 6, specimen Uwe Schwarz 6231
entries.captionEn: The actual Bazzania globuliformis specimen illustrated in its 2023 scientific description. The collection was made near Lake Kasudsuran in August 2000; these micrographs are not a present-day visitor sighting.
entries.altEn: Scientific plate showing the small pale-green leafy liverwort Bazzania globuliformis and magnified leaf structures, with red scale bars.
entries.authorCredit: Uwe Schwarz, Alfons Schäfer-Verwimp and James R. Shevock; Frahmia 33 (2023), Plate 6
entries.modifications: Original PDF page rendered as PNG without changes to the scientific figure.
entries.editorialCaution: Scientific microscopy and field images, not a casual macro photograph; retain the label, scale bars, full attribution, license link and specimen context. Owner, local and native-language review still pending.

entries.subject: The 2018 Lake Janagdan road-route petition or an authorized redacted petition excerpt
entries.locator: Photograph overlaid with a red X on the original 2018 Save Lake Janagdan petition, started by Hanzel Federicos
entries.captionEn: The 2018 Save Lake Janagdan petition illustrated its opposition to a road route with this crossed-out groundworks photograph. The photo does not independently confirm the exact pictured location or project outcome.
entries.altEn: Earthworks and rocks on a forested route, marked with a large red X on the 2018 Save Lake Janagdan petition.
entries.authorCredit: Save Lake Janagdan petition, Hanzel Federicos / Change.org; original image creator not identified
entries.modifications: Original displayed petition image downloaded without alterations.
entries.editorialCaution: Treat as the campaign's illustration, not proof that the pictured works happened at Lake Janagdan. No signatures or private petition information is reproduced.

entries.subject: Naungan–San Juan mangrove planting, 2014 recovery nursery or 2017 reserve development
entries.locator: Shellwanders's 2023 illustrated guide to Ormoc Mangrove Eco-Park, Naungan boardwalk photo
entries.captionEn: The boardwalk at Ormoc Mangrove Eco-Park in Naungan, photographed for a 2023 site guide. This later view illustrates the landscape cared for after Typhoon Haiyan, not the 2014 nursery itself.
entries.altEn: Twilight photograph of the white-railed mangrove boardwalk beside trees and a sandy track at Ormoc Mangrove Eco-Park, Naungan.
entries.authorCredit: Shellwanders, Ormoc Mangrove Eco-Park visitor guide (2023)
entries.modifications: Original photograph copied at article resolution without alterations.
entries.editorialCaution: Exact Naungan Ormoc site, not the different Paraiso Mangrove park in Tacloban. Do not claim this image documents the 2014 post-Yolanda cash-for-work activity.

entries.subject: Ormoc Piña Festival street performance, 2019
entries.locator: Wikimedia Commons original photo dated 23 June 2019
entries.captionEn: A performer at Ormoc's Piña Festival in 2019, two years after the first festival described in the History panel.
entries.altEn: Piña Festival dancer holding a pineapple, in front of a procession of performers in green and orange costumes.
entries.editorialCaution: This photograph shows 2019, NOT the inaugural 2017 Piña Festival or the Sal’s Biliboy farm. Observe share-alike if adapted and seek owner/privacy review for app distribution.

entries.subject: 1994 convention program noting the Leyte Golf competition
entries.locator: The Cable Tow, November–December 1994, printed page 53 (PDF page 55), upper-left paragraph
entries.captionEn: A 1994 issue of The Cable Tow mentions golf competitions at Leyte Golf and Country Club in its Ormoc convention account. The notice is an event record, not a course founding document.
entries.altEn: Scanned 1994 magazine page; opening paragraph says delegates were organized for golf competitions at Leyte Golf and Country Club.
entries.authorCredit: The Cable Tow, Grand Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of the Philippines, Nov–Dec 1994, p. 53
entries.modifications: Printed source page rendered as PNG without altering text.
entries.editorialCaution: The scanned page also contains unrelated text; let users zoom. Do not imply the account establishes when the golf course was created.

entries.subject: Historic Cabintan/Alto Peak approach and disused geothermal drilling area
entries.locator: Gideon Lasco's first-person 2010 ascent, photograph of walkers on the old approach road
entries.captionEn: Walkers on the older Alto Peak approach during Gideon Lasco's 2010 ascent. The historical route passed a disused geothermal drilling site; this is not current trail guidance.
entries.altEn: Four hikers with backpacks walking up a grassy track between thick vegetation on the 2010 Alto Peak approach.
entries.modifications: Original article photograph copied without alterations, including existing watermark.
entries.editorialCaution: Historical site account only. A 2010 trail photograph is not a safe current route or an authorized AR entry point.

entries.subject: Heaven's Peak sunflowers as pictured in the 2019 visitor account
entries.captionEn: The sunflower beds at Heaven's Peak pictured in a local May 2019 visitor post. This is a dated view, not a promise of blooms during today's visit.
entries.altEn: Yellow sunflowers in garden rows with a small pavilion at Heaven's Peak, in a photo published May 2019.
entries.authorCredit: Lucia1397 / LAAG TA (Suroy Ormocanons), 5 May 2019; individual photographer not confirmed
entries.modifications: Original article image copied without alteration.
entries.editorialCaution: This is an archival 2019 view; no claim is made about current flowers, seasons, owner, business hours or access.

entries.subject: Archival Sal's Beach bamboo-and-nipa huts before the Sabin hotel development
entries.locator: Image reproduced on Sabin Resort Hotel tourism page from a 2013-era photograph
entries.captionEn: Sabin Resort Hotel after its development, in a photograph published around 2013. The older Sal's Beach bamboo-and-nipa huts mentioned in the History are not shown.
entries.altEn: Sabin Resort Hotel's two-story veranda building and thatched pool gazebo, amid palms, in an older post-development photograph.
entries.authorCredit: Ephraim Arriesgado (copyright watermark); photo shown on Sabin Resort Hotel tourism page
entries.modifications: Original dated article image copied with visible photographer watermark.
entries.editorialCaution: A post-development view cannot illustrate the original beach huts or certify the hotel's 1990 opening. A genuine pre-hotel archival photo is still welcome later.
